work_order.understanding:
The previous plan's diagnosis of the /approvals overflow was right, and its fix works: all eight of its own acceptance criteria passed on the merits. What it got wrong is the trade it made inside that fix, and the fact that it pinned the trade.

`min-width: 0` on `.approval-actions input` is what let the row shrink past the input's ~234px automatic minimum, so the page stopped overflowing. But `flex: 1` is `flex: 1 1 0%` — a 0% basis — and both buttons carry `min-width: 44px`. So once the automatic minimum is removed, the input is the only item in the row that can give way, and it absorbs the entire shrink deficit. At 414px the row still fits on one line, so `flex-wrap: wrap` never fires, and the field lands at 61px: 59px of client width, six characters, the placeholder rendering as "Rea". At 320 and 375 the wrap does fire and the field gets 108px and 133px instead. The plan predicted this in its own `risks` ("lets it get narrower than its Reason placeholder at a 320px viewport"), called it cosmetic, and shipped it. It is not cosmetic: 414 is one of the three widths issue #71 names as its targets, and the base commit measures 232px at that width, so the fix made the field worse than before at a width the ticket is about.

The worse half is that the plan also pinned the defect. `test/web/pages.test.js` asserts, today, that `.approval-actions input` declares `min-width: 0`, with the message "or the input's ~234px intrinsic width floors the card and the page overflows again". I removed `min-width: 0` from a scratch copy and the suite went red telling me to put the regression back. A green test is currently defending BUG-1. That is why a second attempt at this plan would not converge: the plan's own artifact enforces the defect.

So this revision does two things the previous one did not. It replaces the pin with one that states the property actually wanted — the field has a readable floor — rather than the declaration that happened to fix the overflow. And it fixes BUG-2, which the previous plan wrote into `out_of_scope` as "the client-rendered journal drawer body ... nothing in this ticket's measurements covers it": a deferred surface with no measurement is a surface with no defect report until someone goes looking, which is exactly what QA did. BUG-2 is the same defect class as the rest of this ticket on a fifth surface, and it is one declaration.

I reproduced all of it rather than reasoning from the numbers. Chromium does start in this sandbox — the previous plan recorded that it did not — so every figure below is measured, not carried forward: the reason field at 106/131/59px client width on the commit under test, 232/257/170px with the fix, the drawer body at 1229px of scrollWidth inside 271px, and the full mutation matrix.

One criterion changes. AC-7 enumerates the mutations that must turn the suite red, and one of them is "removing `min-width: 0` from `.approval-actions input`" — a declaration this change deletes, so as written it is no longer performable. I keep AC-7's id, its position and its other five mutations, and restate that one against the new declaration (verified red). Its "66 pass / 0 fail" becomes 67, because the change adds one test. That is the criterion following the code, not the code following the criterion: the criterion's own rule is "each of these mutations turns it red", and the enumerated mutation will not exist after this change. No other criterion is touched, and none is renumbered or dropped.
work_order.root_cause: The /approvals overflow was fixed by removing the reason input's automatic minimum rather than by making the row able to wrap, and the two properties were then pinned as if they were the same one. `flex: 1` gives the input a 0% basis and the two buttons keep `min-width: 44px`, so with `min-width: 0` the field is the only shrinkable item in the row: it absorbs the whole deficit, measuring 59px at a 414px viewport against 232px on the base commit. `flex-wrap: wrap` — the declaration that was supposed to keep the field usable — cannot help at 414, because the row still fits on one line there and the wrap never fires. The test then required `min-width: 0` by name, so the regression is enforced by a green suite rather than caught by one. The same incompleteness has a second instance: the wrap rule was scoped to four server-rendered card lists, and the journal decision drawer renders the same stored free text client-side, so it was deferred into out_of_scope and left measuring 1229px of content inside 271px.
work_order.approach:
Two CSS declarations and two test edits, all four verified in a scratch copy against a live browser and against the suite.

CSS, in two places:
- `.approval-actions input`: `min-width: 0` becomes `min-width: 16ch`. This is the whole of the BUG-1 fix. The overflow does not come back because `flex-wrap: wrap` on `.approval-actions` — already there, already correct — is what actually lets the row shrink; the input never needed its automatic minimum removed, it needed a floor small enough to wrap against and large enough to read. The comment above `.approval-actions` is rewritten to say so, because the old one names `min-width: 0` as the declaration that does the work, which is the wrong lesson and the reason the next reader would repeat it.
- `.journal-drawer-body`: gains `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, the BUG-2 fix. Same property, same value and the same reason as the four card classes; this is the fifth surface that shows stored free text, and it is reached client-side rather than by a server render, which is why no test had ever displayed it.

Nothing else in the stylesheet changes, nothing is reordered, and no other rule is touched.

Test, in test/web/pages.test.js, two edits:
- The `.approval-actions input` pin is rewritten. It required `min-width: 0` by name; it now requires exactly one `min-width` declaration whose value is a plain ch/rem/px length of 12 or more. The failure messages carry the measurement that explains the number, so the next person reading a red suite learns that `min-width: 0` means 59px at 414 rather than having to rediscover it. The `flex-wrap: wrap` pin beside it and the render cross-check are unchanged.
- One new test after it pins `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.journal-drawer-body`. Its comment states plainly that this pin cannot be cross-checked against rendered markup the way the card pin is, because the drawer body is empty in the server's HTML by design — that gap is the reason BUG-2 survived, and hiding it would repeat the mistake.

Measured, on a scratch copy of the PR branch with both changes applied, against a live headless Chromium:
- reason field client width at 320 / 375 / 414: 232 / 257 / 170px (23 / 25.4 / 16.9 characters) against 106 / 131 / 59px (10.6 / 13.1 / 6.0) on the commit under test and 232px at 414 on the base commit. At 600, 900 and 1100 the field is 247, 547 and 731px, byte-identical to the commit under test, so the 1100px layout does not move.
- document scrollWidth == innerWidth and zero offenders outside `.table-scroll` on all five routes at 320, 375 and 414, with the long tenant name, long learning claim, 120-character opportunity and experiment names and two approval cards in the database.
- the `/` `.table-scroll` regions read 494/519/363/620/450 against 238/293/332 and `/journal` 755 — identical to the AC-5 baseline, so the wrap rule has not reached the tables.
- drawer body scrollWidth == clientWidth at 320 / 375 / 414 (271 / 326 / 365) against 1229 before, with zero elements past the viewport's right edge inside the drawer.
- `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` is 67 pass / 0 fail and `node --test` is 307 pass / 0 fail. Each of the six AC-7 mutations turns the page suite red, dropping the drawer declaration turns it red, and the `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` negative case stays green.

files.why: BUG-1 and BUG-2. `min-width: 0` is the declaration that let the only shrinkable item in the row absorb the whole deficit; `overflow-wrap: anywhere` is missing from the one surface that renders stored free text client-side and so was never measured.

The pin this replaces required `min-width: 0` by name, so the suite was green in defence of BUG-1 and removing the regression turned the build red. It must state the readable floor the product needs, and the drawer needs a pin of its own because no render in any test has ever displayed it.

cases: the rewritten `.approval-actions input` pin reproduces BUG-1: with `min-width: 0` on the input the suite goes red on "floors the field at 12 characters or more, or it collapses to six characters of what a human is typing" — run, 65 pass / 1 fail
the same pin with `min-width: 8ch` — below the twelve-character floor — is red, 65 pass / 1 fail
the same pin with `min-width: auto` is red, because the value must be a length that can be measured, 65 pass / 1 fail
the same pin is green on `min-width: 16ch` and stays green if the value is later raised to 18ch or restated as 160px, so the pin states a property and not a literal
the unchanged `flex-wrap: wrap` pin on `.approval-actions` is still red when the declaration is removed, so the two halves of the constraint are both guarded
the new `.journal-drawer-body` pin reproduces BUG-2: with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` removed from that rule the suite goes red, 66 pass / 1 fail
the new drawer pin is green as written, taking the page suite to 67 pass / 0 fail and the full `node --test` run to 307 pass / 0 fail

evidence: Reproduced on the commit under test (c6d30f2) with headless Chromium, the PR branch booted on localhost:3010 against a seeded database plus one approval.requested envelope. The reason input's clientWidth is 106, 131 and 59 at 320, 375 and 414 — QA's figures to the decimal — with computed `flex: 1 1 0%` and `min-width: 0px`, Approve 109.6x44 and Reject 95.4x44, and document scrollWidth equal to innerWidth at all three.

The mechanism, measured rather than inferred: `.approval-actions` is 234 / 259 / 298px wide at 320 / 375 / 414, the two buttons plus two 16px gaps are 237px, and `flex-wrap: wrap` fires at 320 and 375 (form height 104, two rows) but not at 414 (height 44, one row). At 414 the input is therefore whatever is left of 298 after 237 — 61px. The three widths the issue names are the three the previous plan never measured.

Fix measured on a scratch copy at src/web/styles.css with `min-width: 16ch`: the field is 234 / 259 / 172.4px (23 / 25.4 / 16.9 characters) at 320 / 375 / 414, and 247 / 547 / 731px at 600 / 900 / 1100 — the last three byte-identical to the commit under test, so the 1100px layout does not move. Buttons unchanged at 109.6x44 and 95.4x44, inside the viewport at every width, no page overflow anywhere.

Ten candidate floor values were measured at 240, 280, 320, 360, 375, 414, 480, 600, 900 and 1100: `min-width: 0` (the commit under test), 8ch, 10ch, 12ch, 16ch, and the basis variants `flex: 1 1 12ch`, `flex: 1 1 160px`, `flex: 1 1 auto` and `flex: 1 0 100%`. `flex: 1 0 100%` was rejected because it gives the field its own row at 1100 too and so restyles the desktop layout. 16ch is the smallest floor that never drops below 16.9 characters at any width from 320 up, and `flex: 1 1 12ch` was rejected because it leaves 375 at 13.1 characters with an odd half-empty line beside it.

240 and 280px viewports overflow on the commit under test and still overflow with the fix, with the buttons partly outside the viewport. That is pre-existing, the issue names 320 / 375 / 414, and it is recorded in `risks` rather than fixed here.

BUG-2 reproduced and fixed. With a decision carrying 120-character evidence_refs, memory_refs, policy_decision_id and worst_reasonable_case, #journal-drawer-body measured scrollWidth 1229 against clientWidth 271 / 326 / 365 at 320 / 375 / 414, with seven elements past the viewport's right edge. With `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.journal-drawer-body`, scrollWidth equals clientWidth at all three and the offender list is empty. The page's own scrollWidth was correct in both cases, because #journal-drawer is position: fixed.

QA's named coverage gap, answered: a second decision whose decision_id is 140 unbreakable characters and whose state_snapshot_id is 90 was created and /journal measured at 320, 375 and 414 with no offenders, so the awaiting list and the calibration panel do not overflow and need no change.

Suite and mutation matrix, run on the scratch copy with both fixes and the rewritten pin: `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` is 67 pass / 0 fail and `node --test` is 307 pass / 0 fail. Red at 65 pass / 1 fail for each of: `min-width: 0`, `min-width: 8ch`, `min-width: auto`, `flex-wrap: nowrap`, dropping `.learning-card` from the wrap rule, renaming it `.learning-cardw`, appending a later `.approval-card { overflow-wrap: break-word; }`, removing `flex-wrap: wrap` from `.approval-actions`, removing `overflow-wrap` from `.tenant-name`, and removing `overflow-wrap` from `.journal-drawer-body`. Green at 67/0 for the `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` negative case.

The five-route regression sweep with the full fixture set loaded — 137-character tenant name, 120-character learning claim, 120-character opportunity and experiment names, two approval cards, the long-ref decision and the 140-character decision_id — reads scrollWidth == innerWidth with zero offenders outside `.table-scroll` on all fifteen route/width combinations, and the `/` regions read 494/238, 519/238, 363/238, 620/238, 450/238 at 320 and the same five against 293 at 375, matching the AC-5 baseline exactly.

The pin this replaces is why a second attempt at the old plan would not converge: on a scratch copy with the fix applied, `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` fails on "the reason input rule 1 declares min-width: 0, or the input's ~234px intrinsic width floors the card and the page overflows again". A green suite currently enforces BUG-1.

BUG-3 is pre-existing and untouched: this PR changes only src/web/styles.css and test/web/pages.test.js. Reading src/web/client.js:120-150 confirms the drawer installs a keydown handler for Escape and none for Tab, and src/web/pages.js:540 shows #journal-drawer carrying role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and no tabindex.
risks: `min-width: 16ch` depends on `ch` resolving against the input's own font, which `font: inherit` ties to the 16px body. A future font change moves the floor proportionally, which is the intent, but the measured 172px at 414 becomes something else and AC-9's character count is the check rather than a pixel count.

The 12-character floor in the test is a judgement, not a measurement: it is the value below which the field is worse than the base commit was, and it leaves headroom under the 16.9 characters the fix delivers. A future change to 10ch would be green in CI and would be caught by AC-9 in the browser, not by the suite.

The two declarations on `.approval-actions` are now a single constraint — a floor is only safe because the wrap exists, and the wrap is only useful because the input can be floored — and CI enforces them in two separate tests. A reader who deletes one and keeps the other gets a red suite in one direction and a broken layout in the other.

The `.journal-drawer-body` pin cannot be cross-checked against rendered markup, because the drawer body is empty in the server's HTML by design. It asserts that the declaration is present; it cannot assert that the selector matches anything. A future rename of `journal-drawer-body` in both client.js and the stylesheet would leave it green. This is stated in the test comment rather than hidden, and it is the same gap that let BUG-2 through in the first place.

The drawer fix reaches the Close button and the drawer's own heading as well as the decision lines, since `overflow-wrap` is inherited. Both carry fixed product copy, so nothing visible changes; a future long heading would wrap rather than scroll, which is the wanted direction.

AC-7's fourth mutation and its pass count are restated because the change deletes the declaration the old text named. If a reviewer reads that as moving the goalposts, the evidence is that the criterion's own rule is "each of these mutations turns it red" and `min-width: 0` no longer exists in the file to be removed; the id, position and other five mutations are untouched, and no criterion was dropped.
out_of_scope: BUG-3, the aria-modal focus escape in the journal decision drawer: the first Tab from the focused Close button lands on the skip link behind the overlay. It predates #71 — this diff touches neither client.js nor the drawer's markup — and it is a focus-management question rather than a layout one, which is a different ticket. It is deliberately not given an acceptance criterion, because QA would then certify a defect it has not been fixed. Recorded here so the next run that finds it knows it was seen: no keydown handler for Tab in src/web/client.js:120-150, and no tabindex on #journal-drawer in src/web/pages.js:540. Whether a focus trap is even right is unresolved: above 900px the drawer is a side panel and the page behind it is visible, so trapping focus there would be wrong. That is a decision for a person, and QA itself rated it p3 and non-blocking.

Viewports narrower than 320px. They overflow on the commit under test and still overflow with the fix, with the buttons partly outside the viewport. The issue names 320, 375 and 414 and the base commit overflows at all three, so this is a pre-existing limit rather than something this change introduced or was asked to remove.
Truncating or shortening the placeholder, or changing the copy of the Approve and Reject buttons. Both are product decisions, not layout ones, and neither is needed now that the field has a floor.

Giving the reason field a textarea, or moving the Approve and Reject buttons to their own row at every width including 1100. `flex: 1 0 100%` was measured and does the second, at the cost of restyling the desktop layout this ticket was told not to touch.

`.awaiting-list li` and the calibration panel on /journal. Measured with a 140-character decision_id and a 90-character state_snapshot_id at 320, 375 and 414 and neither overflows, so the probe QA named as its open coverage gap is now closed rather than carried.
Any change to src/web/client.js, src/web/pages.js, the API, or the domain. This revision is two CSS declarations and two test edits.

The previous plan put any change to the 1100px layout out of scope and nothing in this issue asks for it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the drawer alone and keep BUG-2 in out_of_scope, as the previous plan did
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is the same reasoning that produced BUG-2: a surface with no measurement is a surface with no defect report until someone probes it, and the fix is one declaration with a measured before and after. `test/web/pages.test.js:1532`

Evidence: Scratch copy at /tmp/p71 on sdlc/issue-71. Baseline: `# pass 66 # fail 0`. Then in src/web/pages.js:73 the opening tag `<span class="tenant-name" id="tenant-name" data-testid="tenant-name">` was replaced with `<span id="tenant-name" data-testid="tenant-name">` (class attribute removed, stylesheet untouched) and `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` was re-run: `# pass 66 # fail 0`. Today the loop is also vacuous: only two rules in src/web/styles.css declare overflow-wrap and both sit before the card rule, so the loop body never executes on the shipped file.

Click the row's open-decision action for that decision

qa.title: Tab escapes the journal decision dialog on the first press, while the dialog is marked aria-modal
qa.expected: A dialog rendered with role="dialog" aria-modal="true" holds focus, or traps it, so a keyboard user is not delivered to page content sitting behind an overlay that claims the rest is unavailable.
qa.actual: On opening a decision the Close button is focused, and the first Tab lands on the skip link outside #journal-drawer, then walks the brand and the five nav links behind it. The drawer is fixed and covers the whole viewport at this width, so the focus ring is drawn on content the user cannot see. #journal-drawer carries no tabindex, so the drawer itself is not a tab stop.
repro: Open /journal at a viewport 900px wide or narrower
Observe focus move to the skip link outside the dialog, which is aria-modal="true"
qa.suspected_cause: src/web/client.js focuses the Close button on open but installs no keydown handler for Tab, so the dialog is announced as modal and behaves as a plain panel. The file's own comment on the error panel shows the focus-on-open pattern is deliberate; the trap is the part that is missing. The contrast with .table-scroll, which the stylesheet gives tabindex="0" precisely so its overflow is keyboard-scrollable, is the closest thing to a precedent in this codebase. Predates #71 -- nothing in this diff touches the drawer.
